transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because after I have these eating episodes, I feel really gross and disappointed in myself. Like I should have more control. I end up writing awful things about myself in my journal afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you do anything to try to prevent weight gain—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?
No, I don’t do anything like that afterward.
How often do these eating episodes happen, and how long has this been going on?
For the past several months, it’s usually happened at least one night a week. I’ll buy too much food after work and eat it all at once. I can’t really remember it stopping for more than a week or so.
During these episodes, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control what or how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah. Once I start, I just keep reaching for the next thing almost automatically. Even if I’m telling myself, “Fumi, stop—you have sketches to finish,” I don’t actually stop until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable.
During these binge episodes, do you notice yourself eating much more quickly than usual, or do you tend to eat alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you're eating?

Yeah, I eat really fast. I’m usually standing at the counter or sitting on my bed with my sketchbook still open, and I barely taste any of it. It’s like I’m trying to get it down before I can think too much.
During these episodes, do you typically keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
I’m not really sure. I know I keep eating for a while, but I haven’t paid much attention to exactly how full I feel.
Thinking back to those episodes, do you usually keep eating even after you already feel very full or overly stuffed?
I’m not sure. I know I eat a lot and feel uncomfortable afterward sometimes, but I haven’t really noticed whether I’m already overly full before I keep going.
